tense.q: By the time we arrived, the film ___.
tense.explain: Past perfect shows an action completed before another past action (arrived).
'Since' + a starting point with a situation continuing to now needs present perfect.

tense.q: I ___ dinner when the phone rang.
tense.explain: Past continuous for an action in progress interrupted by a shorter past action.

tense.q: This time next week, we ___ on a beach.
tense.explain: Future continuous describes an action in progress at a future moment.
Simple present for habits; third person singular takes -s.
Future perfect: completed before a future time ('by 2030').
A finished time word ('yesterday') requires simple past.

tense.q: They ___ for two hours when it began to rain.
tense.explain: Past perfect continuous: duration of an action before another past event.

tense.q: She is exhausted because she ___ all day.
tense.explain: Present perfect continuous links a long activity to its present result (being tired).

tense.q: No sooner ___ the door than the phone rang.
tense.explain: 'No sooner' at the start of a sentence needs inversion with past perfect: no sooner had + subject + V3 + than.

tense.q: I will text you as soon as I ___ home.
tense.explain: After time words (as soon as, when, before), use the present simple for the future.

modals.q: You ___ see a doctor about that cough; it's been weeks.
___ I open the window? It's hot in here.
modals.explain: 'Shall I...?' offers or asks for a suggestion.

modals.q: You ___ pay now; you can pay later.
You ___ smoke here; it is prohibited.
When I was young, I ___ swim across this river.
He ___ have taken the keys; I can't find them anywhere.
modals.explain: 'Might have + V3' = past possibility. 'Ought' would need 'to'.

modals.q: I ___ have told her the truth, but I didn't.
modals.explain: 'Should have + V3' expresses regret or an unfulfilled duty.

modals.q: If I were you, I ___ accept the offer.
modals.explain: Second conditional uses 'would' in the main clause.

modals.q: He ___ have left already; his coat isn't here.
modals.explain: 'Must have + V3' expresses a strong logical deduction about the past.

modals.q: You ___ have bought a gift; I had already got one.
modals.explain: 'Needn't have + V3' means you did something that was not necessary.

modals.q: I would rather you ___ smoke here.
modals.explain: 'Would rather' + subject + past simple expresses a preference about someone else's action.

passive.q: The window ___ by the boy yesterday.
Passive of 'They are building a bridge.'
passive.explain: Present continuous passive: is/are being + V3.
Past perfect passive: had been + V3.
After 'make' in the passive, the bare infinitive becomes a to-infinitive.

options: By whom was this novel written?
By whom this novel was written?
Who was written by this novel?
By whom is this novel wrote?
passive.answer: By whom was this novel written?
passive.explain: Wh-question passive: By whom + was + subject + V3?

passive.q: The house ___ painted at the moment.
passive.explain: Present continuous passive: is being + V3.

passive.q: The manager is believed ___ the company last year.
passive.explain: Passive reporting structure for a past event: is believed + to have + V3.
After 'like' the passive gerund is 'being + V3'.

passive.q: Passive of 'People say that he is rich.'
options: He is said to be rich.
It said that he is rich.
He is said that he is rich.
He was said to be rich.
passive.answer: He is said to be rich.
passive.explain: 'People say that...' becomes 'He is said to + infinitive'.

options: He said that he was tired.
He said that I was tired.
He said that he is tired.
He said that he had been tired.
narration.answer: He said that he was tired.
narration.explain: Reporting verb in past: present → past, pronoun I → he.

narration.q: She said to me, "Where do you live?" → Indirect:
options: She asked me where I lived.
She asked me where did I live.
She told me where I lived.
She asked me where do I live.
narration.answer: She asked me where I lived.
narration.explain: Reported questions use statement word order, with no auxiliary 'do'.

narration.q: The teacher said, "The earth moves round the sun." → Indirect:
options: The teacher said that the earth moves round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth moved round the sun.
The teacher said that earth had moved round the sun.
The teacher told that the earth moves round the sun.
narration.answer: The teacher said that the earth moves round the sun.
narration.explain: Universal truths keep the present tense in reported speech.

narration.q: He said to me, "Please help me." → Indirect:
options: He requested me to help him.
He said me to help him.
He requested me that I help him.
He asked that please help him.
narration.answer: He requested me to help him.

narration.q: "Let's go for a walk," said Ravi. → Indirect:
options: Ravi suggested that they should go for a walk.
Ravi said let us go for a walk.
Ravi ordered them to go for a walk.
Ravi suggested to go for a walk.
narration.answer: Ravi suggested that they should go for a walk.

narration.q: She said, "I will call you tomorrow." → Indirect:
options: She said that she would call me the next day.
She said that she will call you tomorrow.
She said that she would call you tomorrow.
She said that she would have called me next day.
narration.answer: She said that she would call me the next day.
narration.explain: will → would, you → me, tomorrow → the next day.

narration.q: He said, "I have finished my work." → Indirect:
options: He said that he had finished his work.
He said that he has finished his work.
He said that he finished his work.
He said that I had finished my work.
narration.answer: He said that he had finished his work.
narration.explain: Present perfect → past perfect; my → his.

narration.q: "Shut the door," he said to me. → Indirect:
options: He ordered me to shut the door.
He said me to shut the door.
He ordered me that shut the door.
He asked that the door shut.
narration.answer: He ordered me to shut the door.

narration.q: He said, "How beautiful the garden is!" → Indirect:
options: He exclaimed that the garden was very beautiful.
He asked how beautiful the garden was.
He said how beautiful the garden is.
He exclaimed how beautiful was the garden.
narration.answer: He exclaimed that the garden was very beautiful.
narration.explain: Exclamations become statements with 'exclaimed that ... very ...'.

narration.q: She said, "If I were you, I would apologise." → Indirect:
options: She said that if she were me, she would apologise.
She said that if she had been me, she would have apologised.
She said that if she was me, she will apologise.
She said that if I were her, I would apologise.
narration.answer: She said that if she were me, she would apologise.
narration.explain: 'Were' (subjunctive) and 'would' do not change in reported speech; only the pronouns change.

narration.q: He said to her, "Will you marry me?" → Indirect:
options: He asked her if she would marry him.
He asked her will she marry him.
He asked her that she would marry him.
He told her if she will marry him.
narration.answer: He asked her if she would marry him.
narration.explain: Yes/no questions are reported with 'if' or 'whether', in statement order.

nonfinites.q: ___ the door, he entered the room.
nonfinites.explain: Perfect participle shows the action finished before the main verb.
In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition and takes a gerund.

nonfinites.q: The boy ___ in the garden is my brother.
nonfinites.explain: Present participle used as a reduced relative clause.

nonfinites.q: She made me ___ the work again.
nonfinites.explain: 'Make' + object takes a bare infinitive in the active voice.

nonfinites.q: He is too weak ___ the box.
I saw the thief ___ over the wall.
nonfinites.explain: Perception verbs ('saw') + object take a bare infinitive.

nonfinites.q: I remember ___ the letter, so it must be in the post.
nonfinites.explain: 'Remember + gerund' = recall a past action; 'remember + to-infinitive' = not forget to do something.

nonfinites.q: He appears ___ his job last month.
nonfinites.explain: Perfect infinitive (to have + V3) shows an action earlier than the main verb.

articles.explain: 'Honest' starts with a vowel sound (silent h), so use 'an'.
Use 'the' for unique things (the sun, the moon).
'University' begins with a /j/ (consonant) sound, so use 'a'.

articles.q: ___ Nile is the longest river in Africa.
The children go to ___ school by bus every day.
articles.explain: No article when 'school' means the activity of studying.
'Hour' starts with a vowel sound (silent h).

prepositions.explain: Use 'in' with years, months and seasons.

prepositions.q: He has been waiting ___ two hours.
prepositions.explain: 'For' + a length of time; 'since' + a starting point.
'Onto' shows movement to the surface of something.

prepositions.q: We arrived ___ the airport at noon.
prepositions.explain: Arrive 'at' a place (airport, station); 'in' a city or country.

conditionals.q: If it rains, we ___ at home.
conditionals.explain: First conditional: if + present, will + verb.

conditionals.q: If I ___ rich, I would travel the world.
conditionals.explain: Second conditional uses 'were' for all subjects in formal English.

conditionals.q: If she had studied, she ___ the exam.
conditionals.explain: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + V3.

conditionals.q: Unless you hurry, you ___ the train.
conditionals.explain: 'Unless' = 'if not'. 'Unless you hurry' means 'if you don't hurry', so you will miss it.

conditionals.q: If you mix red and blue, you ___ purple.
conditionals.explain: Zero conditional (general truths): if + present, present.

conditionals.q: I wish I ___ more free time.
conditionals.explain: 'Wish' + past simple for an unreal present situation.

conditionals.q: If he ___ earlier, he wouldn't have missed the bus.
conditionals.explain: Third conditional needs past perfect in the if-clause.

conditionals.q: ___ I known, I would have helped.
conditionals.explain: Inverted third conditional: 'Had I known' = 'If I had known'.

agreement.q: Each of the students ___ a book.

agreement.explain: Subjects ending in -ics (mathematics, physics) are singular.

agreement.q: The police ___ looking for the thief.
Either the teacher or the students ___ responsible.
agreement.explain: With either...or, the verb agrees with the nearer subject (students).

agreement.q: One of my friends ___ a doctor.

agreement.explain: 'News' looks plural but is uncountable and singular.

agreement.q: A number of students ___ absent today.
agreement.explain: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb ('The number of' takes singular).

relatives.q: The man ___ lives next door is a doctor.
relatives.explain: 'Who' is the subject relative pronoun for people.

relatives.q: This is the book ___ I told you about.
She is the girl ___ father is a pilot.
That's the house ___ I was born.
He is the man to ___ I gave the money.
I know the reason ___ she left.
My brother, ___ lives in Pune, is an engineer.
relatives.explain: In non-defining clauses (with commas) 'that' is not used.

comparison.explain: Short adjectives take -er in the comparative.

comparison.q: This is the ___ book I have ever read.
He is the ___ of the three brothers.
She is as ___ as her mother.
comparison.explain: 'As ... as' uses the base form of the adjective.

comparison.q: This problem is ___ than that one.
The more you practise, ___ you become.
comparison.explain: Double comparative: the + comparative, the + comparative.
'Fast' is both adjective and adverb; its comparative is 'faster'.

conjunctions.q: He was tired, ___ he kept working.
___ it was raining, we went out.
Hurry up, ___ you will miss the bus.
She didn't come ___ she was ill.
I will call you ___ I reach home.
conjunctions.explain: 'As soon as' links two actions in time.

conjunctions.q: He works hard ___ he can pass the exam.
Neither Tom ___ Jerry attended the party.
You can't go out ___ you finish your homework.

tags.explain: A positive statement takes a negative tag with the same auxiliary.
A negative statement takes a positive tag.
Repeat the modal verb in the tag.
'I am' takes the special tag 'aren't I'.
Repeat the auxiliary 'have' in negative form.
'Nobody' is negative in meaning, so use a positive tag with 'they'.

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: वह रोज़ स्कूल जाता है।
options: He goes to school every day.
He is going to school every day.
He went to school every day.
He has gone to school every day.
translation.answer: He goes to school every day.
translation.explain: A daily habit uses the Simple Present; with 'he' the verb takes -s (goes). (Type: Simple sentence, Simple Present)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: मैं एक किताब पढ़ता हूँ।
translation.answer: I read a book.
translation.explain: 'पढ़ता हूँ' is the Simple Present: subject + V1. (Type: Simple sentence, Simple Present)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: राम ने कल एक फ़िल्म देखी।
options: Ram has watched a film yesterday.
Ram will watch a film yesterday.
translation.answer: Ram watched a film yesterday.
translation.explain: A finished past action ('yesterday') takes the Simple Past: watched. (Type: Simple sentence, Simple Past)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: वह एक डॉक्टर है।
translation.answer: He is a doctor.
translation.explain: 'है' = is. Use the article 'a' before a profession. (Type: Simple sentence, Simple Present (verb 'to be'))

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: मैं हर सुबह टहलने जाता हूँ।
options: I go for a walk every morning.
I am going for a walk every morning.
I went for a walk every morning.
I have gone for a walk every morning.
translation.answer: I go for a walk every morning.
translation.explain: 'हर सुबह' (every morning) shows a habit, so use the Simple Present. (Type: Simple sentence, Simple Present)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: बच्चे पार्क में खेल रहे हैं।
options: The children are playing in the park.
The children play in the park.
The children played in the park.
The children have played in the park.
translation.answer: The children are playing in the park.
translation.explain: 'खेल रहे हैं' (action happening now) = is/are + V-ing. (Type: Tense, Present Continuous)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: मैं अगले सप्ताह दिल्ली जाऊँगा।
options: I will go to Delhi next week.
I go to Delhi next week.
I went to Delhi next week.
I have gone to Delhi next week.
translation.answer: I will go to Delhi next week.
translation.explain: 'जाऊँगा' is the future: will + V1. (Type: Tense, Simple Future)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: मैं आजकल अंग्रेज़ी सीख रहा हूँ।
options: I am learning English these days.
I am learn English these days.
I was learning English these days.
translation.answer: I am learning English these days.
translation.explain: A temporary, ongoing activity: am + V-ing. (Type: Tense, Present Continuous)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: वह तैर सकता है।
translation.answer: He can swim.
translation.explain: 'सकता है' expresses ability: can + V1. (Type: Modal, can (ability))

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: क्या मैं अंदर आ सकता हूँ?
translation.answer: Can I come in?
translation.explain: A request for permission uses a modal: Can I...? (Type: Modal, can (permission))

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: तुम्हें रोज़ पढ़ाई करनी चाहिए।
translation.answer: You should study every day.
translation.explain: 'चाहिए' = should; it gives advice. (Type: Modal, should (advice))

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: आपको यहाँ धूम्रपान नहीं करना चाहिए।
translation.answer: You should not smoke here.
translation.explain: 'नहीं करना चाहिए' = should not + V1. (Type: Modal, should not (advice))

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: मुझे सुबह जल्दी उठना है।
options: I have to get up early in the morning.
I get up early in the morning.
I got up early in the morning.
I have got up early in the morning.
translation.answer: I have to get up early in the morning.
translation.explain: 'मुझे ... उठना है' expresses necessity: have to + V1 (a semi-modal). (Type: Modal, have to (obligation))

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: मैंने अभी खाना खाया है।
options: I have just eaten my meal.
I am just eating my meal.
I had just eaten my meal.
translation.answer: I have just eaten my meal.
translation.explain: A recent action with a present result: have/has + V3 (with 'just'). (Type: Tense, Present Perfect)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: जब तुमने फ़ोन किया, मैं खाना बना रहा था।
options: I was cooking when you called.
I am cooking when you called.
I have been cooking when you called.
translation.answer: I was cooking when you called.
translation.explain: An action in progress in the past, interrupted by another: was/were + V-ing. (Type: Tense, Past Continuous)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: वह सोमवार से बीमार है।
options: He has been ill since Monday.
He had been ill since Monday.
translation.answer: He has been ill since Monday.
translation.explain: 'Since' + a point in time with a situation continuing now needs the Present Perfect. (Type: Tense, Present Perfect)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: यह किताब मेरे दोस्त ने लिखी थी।
options: This book was written by my friend.
This book wrote by my friend.
This book is written by my friend.
This book has written by my friend.
translation.answer: This book was written by my friend.
translation.explain: Passive: was/were + V3 (written), with 'by' for the doer. (Type: Passive, Simple Past passive)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: अंग्रेज़ी पूरी दुनिया में बोली जाती है।
options: English is spoken all over the world.
English speaks all over the world.
English is speaking all over the world.
English spoke all over the world.
translation.answer: English is spoken all over the world.
translation.explain: Passive: is/are + V3 (spoken). (Type: Passive, Simple Present passive)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: अगर बारिश हुई तो हम घर पर रहेंगे।
options: If it rains, we will stay at home.
If it will rain, we will stay at home.
If it rained, we will stay at home.
If it rains, we would stayed at home.
translation.answer: If it rains, we will stay at home.
translation.explain: A real future possibility: If + Present Simple, will + V1. (Type: Conditional, First conditional)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: उसने कहा कि वह थका हुआ है।
options: He said that he was tired.
He said that I am tired.
He said that he will be tired.
He said that he were tired.
translation.answer: He said that he was tired.
translation.explain: After a past reporting verb, the present tense shifts back to the past: is tired → was tired. (Type: Narration, Reported statement)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: बचपन में मैं बहुत तेज़ दौड़ सकता था।
options: When I was a child, I could run very fast.
In my childhood I can run very fast.
When I was a child, I should run very fast.
In my childhood I must have run very fast.
translation.answer: When I was a child, I could run very fast.
translation.explain: 'सकता था' = could: general ability in the past. (Type: Modal, could (past ability))

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: वह अब तक घर पहुँच गया होगा।
options: He must have reached home by now.
He must reach home by now.
He will reach home by now.
He has reached home by now.
translation.answer: He must have reached home by now.
translation.explain: 'होगा' (a guess about the past) = must have + V3. (Type: Modal, must have + V3 (deduction))

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: आपको मेरी मदद करनी चाहिए थी।
translation.answer: You should have helped me.
translation.explain: 'चाहिए थी' = should have + V3: something that was not done. (Type: Modal, should have + V3 (regret))

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: वह पिछले दो घंटे से पढ़ रहा है।
options: He has been studying for the last two hours.
He is studying since two hours.
He had studied for two hours.
translation.answer: He has been studying for the last two hours.
translation.explain: An action that started in the past and is still going on: has/have been + V-ing, with 'for'. (Type: Tense, Present Perfect Continuous)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: जब मैं पहुँचा, ट्रेन जा चुकी थी।
options: When I arrived, the train had already left.
When I arrived, the train has already left.
When I arrive, the train had already left.
When I arrived, the train would already leave.
translation.answer: When I arrived, the train had already left.
translation.explain: The earlier of two past actions takes the Past Perfect: had + V3. (Type: Tense, Past Perfect)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: अगले साल तक वह अपनी पढ़ाई पूरी कर चुका होगा।
options: By next year, he will have completed his studies.
By next year, he will complete his studies.
By next year, he has completed his studies.
By next year, he would have completed his studies.
translation.answer: By next year, he will have completed his studies.
translation.explain: An action finished before a future time: will have + V3. (Type: Tense, Future Perfect)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: नया पुल बनाया जा रहा है।
options: A new bridge is being built.
translation.answer: A new bridge is being built.
translation.explain: Passive of the Present Continuous: is/are being + V3. (Type: Passive, Present Continuous passive)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: अगर मेरे पास पैसे होते तो मैं घूमने जाता।
options: If I had money, I would go on a trip.
If I have money, I will go on a trip.
If I had money, I will go on a trip.
If I would have money, I would go on a trip.
translation.answer: If I had money, I would go on a trip.
translation.explain: An unreal present situation: If + Past Simple, would + V1. (Type: Conditional, Second conditional)

translation.q: Translate this Hindi sentence into English.
translation.hindi: उसने मुझसे पूछा कि मैं कहाँ रहता हूँ।
options: He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where I will live.
He asked me where I had lived.
translation.answer: He asked me where I lived.
translation.explain: Reported questions use statement word order (no 'did') and shift the tense back: live → lived. (Type: Narration, Reported question)
